title: Proxy & Orchestration SDK fit check - Elysian Ventures
summary: Initial integration discovery for Elysian Ventures evaluating Redwood for inference. They run a LangChain-first stack with an internal gateway, need EU data residency, want to understand SDK integration options, proxy/sidecar patterns, throttle/quota behavior, and observability hooks. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and proposed pilot plan and next steps.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07 10:00 UTC | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Tom Hale (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO, Elysian), Lena Morales (Eng Mgr), Ivy Chen (Platform), Samir Bose (Security)

[00:00] Tom Hale: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:05] Raj Patel: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Tom.
[00:08] Tom Hale: Cool. Goal for today is to understand your integration surface — SDKs, Lang Chain/LlamaIndex usage, gateway patterns — and walk through tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private. We'll capture next steps at the end. Maya, Omar you want to intro?
[00:22] Maya Chen: Sure — Maya, Redwood SE. I'll focus on technical fit, SDKs and observable hooks. Omar will cover security/eu region onboarding.
[00:27] Omar Ruiz: Hey all.
[00:28] Lena Morales: Quick context from us — we run a Lang Chain heavy stack, some homegrown connectors to LlamaIndex, and a central gateway that routes to different model endpoints. We're evaluating Redwood for lower latency and predictable costs.
[00:43] Ivy Chen: Also EU data residency requirement for a subset of requests — for GDPR compliance.
[00:47] Tom Hale: Got it. Raj, what's the timeline and success criteria?
[00:51] Raj Patel: Timeline's roughly 2-3 months for a pilot. Success is: p95 latency under 150ms for short completions (under 256 tokens), predictable token costs, and ability to route EU traffic to EU region with audit logs.
[01:06] Maya Chen: OK that's helpful. On the SDK side: Redwood has Python and Node SDKs, and a REST interface. For Lang Chain we provide connectors — sample code plus a small adapter that acts like an LLM object. For LlamaIndex (sometimes called Llama-Indexer internally) we have examples but some naming in the transcript might be fuzzy — it's LlamaIndex.
[01:29] Lena Morales: Great. We currently use Lang Chain 0.3x with custom prompts and a local caching layer. How invasive is the integration? Do we swap clients or put Redwood behind our gateway?
[01:40] Maya Chen: Two common patterns: 1) Gateway-proxy pattern — keep your gateway routing to Redwood endpoints directly (REST/HTTP or SDK calls). 2) Sidecar/adapter inside services — embed Redwood SDK in the service runtime so you get direct calls and local KV caching. Both are supported. The gateway approach is easier for a pilot.
[01:58] Samir Bose: On security — if we start hosted, do you do EU-only hosting and separation? What about key management and K-M-S?
[02:07] Omar Ruiz: Yes, we have hosted EU regions and you can restrict processing to EU. For key management we support customer-managed keys via KMS/H-S-M integrations in Dedicated/Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with customer-owned keys for certain tiers. We'll send the security pack.
[02:28] Raj Patel: Is there a big difference in latency between hosted and dedicated? We need to know if hosted can hit that 150ms p95 for our use case.
[02:36] Maya Chen: It depends on model choice, sequence length, and tokenization overhead. For short prompts with tuned models in EU hosted, many customers see sub-150ms p95 on our smaller text-generation models. Dedicated improves predictability — reserved GPU pools, lower jitter, and custom kernel selection. If you want strict SLOs and consistent throughput, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[03:01] Lena Morales: We also want to run some reranking and embeddings at scale — burst capacity matters. How do rate limits and quotas work?
[03:10] Maya Chen: We enforce per-account and per-route quotas. There are global rate limits and token quotas. For Dedicated you get configurable burst windows and higher default quotas. We can also set route-level rate limits so you can throttle embedding-heavy calls to a separate pool.
[03:28] Tom Hale: Another option is to do hybrid: start Hosted for EU region pilot, then move to Dedicated once you prove throughput and want reserved capacity.
[03:38] Raj Patel: If we piped everything through our gateway, are there observability hooks we can use to correlate requests end-to-end?
[03:45] Omar Ruiz: Yes — we emit trace IDs, per-token cost metrics, and request/response timing. You can push these into your existing tracing (OpenTelemetry) or pull via our observability API. We also expose token-level breakdowns and latency percentiles per model and per-route.
[04:03] Ivy Chen: Are there SDK-level hooks for token streaming and partial responses? We depend on streaming for chat.
[04:10] Maya Chen: SDKs support streaming and function/tool style streaming. There's also a streaming websocket path if you need very low-latency incremental tokens. Some transcription artifacts: sometimes "K-V cache" shows up as "K-V cash" in notes — but it's the same KV cache semantics.
[04:28] Raj Patel: Any gotchas with Lang Chain or LlamaIndex wrappers? We use LlamaIndex heavily for retrieval-augmented generation.
[04:35] Maya Chen: In our Lang Chain adapter we keep the interface similar. For LlamaIndex you might need a small shim for indices that rely on local file-based stores; cloud-based vector stores map directly to the embeddings endpoints. We have example notebooks for LlamaIndex + Redwood embeddings and a sample pipeline for hybrid search + generation. We'll share the repo.
[04:58] Lena Morales: What about cost controls? We want to avoid runaway costs during dev.
[05:03] Tom Hale: There are a few levers: route-level quotas, per-key rate limits, token budget alerts, and auto-fallback to smaller models. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching to cut unit cost. For pilots, we'd recommend a guardrail quota + alerts.
[05:20] Raj Patel: For the pilot sizing: what information do you need from us?
[05:24] Maya Chen: Typical asks: monthly token estimate, concurrent requests, typical prompt lengths, and embedding vs generation split. Also what percent of traffic must stay in EU vs global.
[05:36] Raj Patel: We can share a rough projection — about 120M tokens/mo initially, 30% embeddings, p95 latency target 150ms for generation under 256 tokens, concurrent ~30 during peak.
[05:52] Maya Chen: Good, that's workable for a small dedicated pool or a hosted pilot with burst capacity.
[05:58] Samir Bose: On compliance, do you maintain audit logs for requests and the ability to redact PII from logs?
[06:05] Omar Ruiz: Yes, audit logs are available and for Dedicated/Private you can disable storage of request payloads. We also offer configurable retention and automated redaction rules. We'll include details in the security pack.
[06:20] Ivy Chen: A bit more on the gateway: we do model routing in our gateway today — sometimes we need to fall back to smaller models when load spikes. Can Redwood handle graceful degradation?
[06:30] Maya Chen: Absolutely — policy-based routing allows fallbacks to compatible model variants and automatic routing by latency or cost. You can pin specific model versions per route. In your gateway you can implement a policy to switch endpoints if latency exceeds a threshold.
[06:48] Raj Patel: Are there prebuilt plugins for common gateway products or do you provide only examples?
[06:53] Maya Chen: Mostly examples and SDK snippets. We have a lightweight proxy sample (NGINX + Lua or node proxy) and example Helm charts for sidecar deployments. For specific gateways we can work with your gateway team to provide a reference integration.
[07:08] Tom Hale: Quick question on dev experience — how fast can engineers onboard and run a small test?
[07:12] Omar Ruiz: For hosted — minutes: API key, SDK install, run sample notebook. For Dedicated/Private, onboarding includes capacity provisioning and optionally VPC setup — that usually takes a few days to a couple weeks depending on approvals.
[07:28] Lena Morales: Can we run our benchmarks against hosted first? We'd like real-world p95 numbers before committing to dedicated.
[07:35] Maya Chen: Yes, that's the recommended path. We can provide a benchmark harness and a thin proxy patch so you can route a percentage of traffic to Redwood for A/B. We'll supply scripts to replay traffic or run synthetic loads.
[07:51] Raj Patel: Any limitations with streaming when behind proxies? We have an existing edge proxy that buffers responses; streaming becomes chunked.
[07:59] Maya Chen: Right — edge proxies often buffer. We recommend either bypassing buffering for streaming routes (route-level config) or use Redwood's websocket streaming which plays nicer with proxies. We'll include notes on streaming best practices.
[08:14] Ivy Chen: How are quotas enforced — per-token or per-request? We need predictable throttling semantics.
[08:21] Maya Chen: We enforce both. There's rate-per-second and token-based quotas. For predictable throttling, token quotas across a sliding window are available. Dedicated customers can customize the windows.
[08:35] Samir Bose: Are SLA terms available for Dedicated?
[08:38] Tom Hale: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in the enterprise contract. We'll include the SLA summary in the proposal.
[08:47] Raj Patel: Any customer references for similar setups?
[08:50] Tom Hale: We can share anonymized reference notes; a couple of fintech customers run a gateway + Redwood hybrid approach for EU traffic. We'll connect you to a reference if needed.
[09:00] Lena Morales: On observability — do you export traces or do we pull them?
[09:04] Omar Ruiz: We support OpenTelemetry and can push traces to your collector or you can pull via our exports. There's a query API for per-token accounting and a per-route dashboard in Console.
[09:17] Raj Patel: Good. Let's talk pilot specifics — what would success look like after 4 weeks?
[09:22] Maya Chen: 4-week pilot success: run a replay of representative traffic, validate p95 latency <150ms on target routes, validate embedding throughput at expected QPS, confirm audit logs and key management, and prove cost per 1M tokens aligns to expected bands.
[09:39] Tom Hale: We're proposing a small hosted EU pilot with guarded quotas, then a follow-on dedicated reservation if pilot metrics meet targets.
[09:47] Raj Patel: Sounds reasonable. Any blockers on our side?
[09:51] Lena Morales: We need the Lang Chain/LlamaIndex examples and a benchmark harness; plus security docs for legal.
[09:58] Tom Hale: We'll send those.
[10:00] Maya Chen: I'll zip up a repo with Lang Chain and LlamaIndex adapters, a sample NGINX proxy config for streaming, and a benchmark harness you can run.
[10:09] Omar Ruiz: I'll attach SOC2, ISO, and the EU region onboarding checklist.
[10:13] Raj Patel: Great. One more operational question — our platform uses ephemeral API keys per service. Can Redwood support short-lived keys and rotating credentials via OIDC or KMS?
[10:23] Maya Chen: Yes — short-lived tokens via OIDC are supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports rotated API keys and we can integrate with your secret store for automation.
[10:34] Samir Bose: For DDoS protection at the gateway layer, if we're routing heavy embedding calls, any recommended controls?
[10:40] Omar Ruiz: Rate-limiting at the gateway, route isolation (separate pool for embeddings), and token budgets with alerts. We'll include recommended patterns in the handoff doc.
[10:50] Lena Morales: Ok, last thing — does Redwood support quantized model flavors to reduce cost?
[10:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we surface quantized variants and recommend them for embedding and some generation workloads. Redwood Optimize can run a quick analysis to suggest quantization levels.
[11:06] Tom Hale: All right — let's recap next steps and owners.
[11:09] Tom Hale: Action items: Tom send pricing + SOW, Maya share repo and benchmark scripts, Omar send security pack. Elysian to provide token projections.
[11:21] Raj Patel: Perfect. We'll aim to have projections to you by 2026-07-09.
[11:26] Tom Hale: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and schedule the pilot kickoff.
[11:32] Lena Morales: Thanks everyone.
[11:34] Meeting end.
